# Streams API

> Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. `ReadableStream`, `WritableStream`, and `TransformStream` are the WHATWG (browser-standard) backbone of pipeline-style data processing. Node has its own, older, differently-shaped `stream` module — see the Node rows below — that real Node code (including `fs`/`http`/`child_process` internally) actually uses far more than the WHATWG API.

**Coverage**: 9/9 (100%) · **Strict Coverage**: 3/9 (~33%).

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format).

Full design: [TDD-00097](../tdd/TDD-00097.md) ([ADR-00296](../adr/00/ADR-00296.md)–[ADR-00302](../adr/00/ADR-00302.md), [ADR-00304](../adr/00/ADR-00304.md)). `pipeTo` (all four shutdown-propagation rules + `prevent*` + `AbortSignal`), `pipeThrough`, and `tee()` come with the rows below; in-memory pipelines run on the promise/microtask runtime alone — no fibers or libcurl. HTTP integration is tracked where it surfaces: fetch `Response.body` on [NETWORKING.md](NETWORKING.md), streaming response/request bodies on [HTTP-SERVER.md](HTTP-SERVER.md).

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ReadableStream` | ✅ | • No BYOB readers / byte controllers (`type: 'bytes'` rejected at compile time)<br>• `ReadableStream.from()` accepts arrays only, not async iterables<br>• Source callbacks must be arrow/function-expression/method-shorthand literals<br>• `read()` on a closed stream whose chunk type is an **array/tuple** (`ReadableStream<number[]>`) yields the chunk's zero-shaped value, not `undefined` (an array slot has no spare absent state — [ADR-00246](../adr/00/ADR-00246.md))<br>• In the no-fiber tier, `await` of an already-settled `read()` skips the microtask drain, so a pending pull can run one tick later than real JS<br>• A synchronously-throwing pull/start propagates to the caller instead of erroring the stream<br>• A signal abort of `pipeTo` takes effect at the next chunk boundary<br>• `pipeThrough`'s argument must be statically a `TransformStream`: one typed `any`, or a plain `{ readable, writable }` pair, is a compile error | • One 144-byte heap struct fuses stream + controller + reader (compile-time retyping), a host header word before it; chunk queue + pending-read promise FIFO with HWM/size accounting; spec CallPullIfNeeded; per-site fulfill thunk builds typed `{value,done}` records ([ADR-00296](../adr/00/ADR-00296.md))<br>• Through `any` a stream keeps its identity and members; console.log renders streams, readers, writers and controllers as Node does, and a released reader or writer rejects its closed/ready and operations with Node's state errors ([ADR-01718](../adr/01/ADR-01718.md))<br>• Runs on the promise/microtask runtime alone — no fibers or libcurl for in-memory pipelines<br>• A scalar/string/object chunk reads a real `undefined`, and `controller.desiredSize` is `null` once errored ([TDD-00196](../tdd/TDD-00196.md), [ADR-00826](../adr/00/ADR-00826.md))<br>• `values()` and `[Symbol.asyncIterator]()` are Node's iterator (buffered fast path, `return()` cancelling with its value, `preventCancel`); a source's `cancel` gets the reason as given, and a `tee()` cancels its source with both branches' reasons ([ADR-01933](../adr/01/ADR-01933.md)) |
| `WritableStream` | ✅ | • A synchronously-throwing sink write propagates instead of erroring the stream (an async rejection is handled per spec)<br>• A sink abort callback can't take a reason parameter; no transformer/sink `start` promise-vs-write interlock beyond the started flag | • 128-byte fused stream+controller+writer struct; 32-byte write-queue entries carry their own per-write promise; `ready` re-armed on backpressure flips ([ADR-00297](../adr/00/ADR-00297.md)) |
| `TransformStream` | ✅ | • A promise a transformer's `start` returns does not delay the first transform<br>• Not Node's backpressure-promise algorithm: a read or write can settle a few microtask ticks earlier<br>• Cancelling the readable side doesn't error the writable side<br>• An identity transform (no callback) whose output chunk type is of another kind converts each chunk to it (`NaN` for a string read as a number), where Node passes it through unchanged ([ADR-01983](../adr/01/ADR-01983.md)) | • Writable sink write runs the transform when the readable side has capacity, else parks the chunk (at most one, by write serialization); readable pull resumes it; spec defaults writable HWM 1 / readable HWM 0 ([ADR-00298](../adr/00/ADR-00298.md)) |
